classification.difficultyReason: Connect symmetric polynomial evaluations to coefficients, then express a reciprocal root sum using Vieta’s formulas.

content.prompt:
Suppose $p$, $q$ and $r$ are the roots of a cubic polynomial $P(x)$. If
$$\frac{P\left(\frac15\right)+P\left(-\frac15\right)}{P(0)}=42,$$
then determine the value of
$$\frac1{pq}+\frac1{pr}+\frac1{qr}.$$

answer.short:
$500$.

The symmetric evaluations determine the ratio of the quadratic coefficient to the constant term; Vieta’s formulas give the required sum as this ratio.
answer.worked:
Write $P(x)=ax^3+bx^2+cx+d$, where $a\ne0$. The given quotient requires $d\ne0$.
$$\begin{align*}P\left(\frac15\right)+P\left(-\frac15\right)&=\left(\frac{a}{125}+\frac{b}{25}+\frac{c}{5}+d\right)+\left(-\frac{a}{125}+\frac{b}{25}-\frac{c}{5}+d\right)\\P\left(\frac15\right)+P\left(-\frac15\right)&=\frac{2b}{25}+2d\\\frac{P\left(\frac15\right)+P\left(-\frac15\right)}{P(0)}&=\frac{2b}{25d}+2\\\frac{2b}{25d}+2&=42\\\frac{b}{d}&=500\end{align*}$$
By Vieta’s formulas, $p+q+r=-\frac{b}{a}$ and $pqr=-\frac{d}{a}$.
$$\begin{align*}\frac1{pq}+\frac1{pr}+\frac1{qr}&=\frac{p+q+r}{pqr}\\\frac1{pq}+\frac1{pr}+\frac1{qr}&=\frac{-b/a}{-d/a}\\\frac1{pq}+\frac1{pr}+\frac1{qr}&=\frac{b}{d}\\\frac1{pq}+\frac1{pr}+\frac1{qr}&=500\end{align*}$$
